facts.raw_span: discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla
severe pruritus at these sites that would wake him up at night
denied any recent trauma or history of similar lesions
denied associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms (eg, fever, chills)
3 well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion that are limited to his right axilla
No other lesions were noted on his skin or mucous membranes
A Wood lamp examination was negative
lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction
treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant yielded no improvement

concepts.why: The presence of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches and lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction on biopsy are characteristic of Granuloma annulare.

The clinical presentation of violaceous, annular patches and the histological finding of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction could be consistent with Sarcoidosis, although the lack of systemic symptoms and other organ involvement makes it less likely.

The presence of well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches and the histological finding of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction could be consistent with Mycosis fungoides, although the lack of other characteristic features such as scale or erosion makes it less likely.

The clinical presentation of violaceous, annular patches and the histological finding of lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction could be consistent with Lichen planus, although the lack of other characteristic features such as scale or mucosal involvement makes it less likely.

The presence of well-circumscribed, annular patches could be consistent with Dermatophytosis, although the negative Wood lamp examination and lack of other characteristic features such as scale or erosion make it less likely.

The presence of severe pruritus and the lack of response to treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream and discontinuation of underarm deodorant could be consistent with Contact dermatitis, although the clinical presentation of violaceous, annular patches is not typical.

rationales.F05: The description of 3 well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion is highly suggestive of Granuloma annulare.
rationales.F08: Lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction is a key histopathological feature of several dermatological conditions, including Granuloma annulare, Sarcoidosis, Mycosis fungoides, and Lichen planus.
